title: Assistive LLM and Design Strategy
subtitle: Simulating Multi-Stakeholder Roundtable Discussions (2025 Master's Graduation Project)

mainContent.content: This project is a master's dissertation from the Design for Performance and Interaction program at University College London (UCL). The research explores an innovative user experience paradigm: a multi-stakeholder roundtable discussion simulation system based on Large Language Models (LLMs). It aims to help designers quickly acquire diverse perspectives during strategy formulation by simulating debates and collaborations among AI Agents with different backgrounds, personalities, and psychological traits. The core of the project lies in constructing a dynamic digital environment and introducing "Intent Visualization," allowing users to intuitively track AI behavioral patterns and decision tendencies without reading massive amounts of text.

Core Pain Points: In traditional design research, collecting and integrating opinions from multiple stakeholders (such as urban planners, environmentalists, residents, etc.) faces significant challenges: information overload, cognitive burden, and data fragmentation.

Solution: Designers' Roundtable System.
- OneAgent (Agent Architecture): Each Agent has an independent memory bank, personality traits, and voting mechanism.
- RoundTable (Roundtable Hub): Serves as the center of collective intelligence, responsible for collecting proposals, organizing votes, and dynamically deciding the next discussion topic based on winning proposals.
- Interactive Interface: 3D roundtable meeting room (immersive visual metaphor), real-time intervention (users can pause meetings at any time).
- Intent Visualization: Uses LLM output Embedding vectors and PCA dimensionality reduction techniques to transform abstract viewpoints into visualizable dot matrices. Trend tracking, stance analysis.

Core Design Thinking:
- From "Dialogue" to "Social Simulation": Moving beyond traditional ChatGPT Q&A mode toward Agent-based social dynamics simulation.
- Visualized "Thought Space": Proposing high-dimensional vector visualization to "see" the direction of discussions and the formation of consensus.
- Human-AI Collaborative "Director Mode": Users are no longer micro-level operators, but macro-level "directors."
